fixes.x: Which small form-factor fiber connector, secured by a latch tab similar to an RJ45 plug, is common in modern high-density switches?
fixes.e: The LC is the small form-factor fiber connector with an RJ45-style latch tab, standard on SFP transceivers and high-density switch line cards. ST is a legacy bayonet-style fiber connector, while F-type and RJ45 terminate copper media, not fiber.
fixes._why: The stem and explanation describe the LC connector using the SC connector's defining characteristics: 'square' body and 'push-pull' coupling belong to SC, while LC is the small form-factor connector secured by an RJ45-style latch tab. [https://thenetworkinstallers.com/blog/lc-vs-sc-fiber-connector/]
